assertions.text: an employee non-solicitation provision is not enforceable against employees working in California
assertions.note: Stated as a categorical rule; the authority is fact-dependent. AMN held the provision void because the restrained activity WAS the former employees' own profession — they were recruiters, and the clause stopped them recruiting: 'This provision clearly restrained individual defendants from practicing with Aya their chosen profession — recruiting travel nurses.' That reasoning does not transfer automatically to an employee whose profession is not recruiting. No decision was located settling the question categorically, and the opinion itself recites the competing common-law reasonableness standard rather than treating the point as closed. The clause converts a contested, fact-sensitive holding into a flat statement of law.

assertions.text: section 16600 voids contractual restraints on a lawful profession, trade, or business
assertions.note: Quoted verbatim by the California Supreme Court in Ixchel.

gaps: The statute opens 'Except as provided in this chapter.' The clause states the rule with no indication that the chapter contains exceptions at all.

The clause says nothing about the carve-outs it does contain — general advertising, employee-initiated contact — being the thing that might save it. If the categorical claim is wrong, those carve-outs are doing the real work and the clause does not say so.

judicialQuotations.case: AMN Healthcare, Inc. v. Aya Healthcare Services, Inc. (Cal. Ct. App. 2018)
judicialQuotations.quote: Turning to the instant case, we independently conclude that the nonsolicitation of employee provision in the CNDA is void under section 16600. Indeed, the broadly worded provision prevents individual defendants, for a period of at least one year after termination of employment with AMN, from either "directly or indirectly" soliciting or recruiting, or causing others to solicit or induce, any employee of AMN. This provision clearly restrained individual defendants from practicing with Aya their chosen profession — recruiting travel nurses on 13-week assignments with AMN.

judicialQuotations.case: Ixchel Pharma, LLC v. Biogen, Inc. (Cal. 2020)
judicialQuotations.quote: The language of section 16600 is broad on its face: "Except as provided in this chapter, every contract by which anyone is restrained from engaging in a lawful profession, trade, or business of any kind is to that extent void."

singleOpinionCaveat: The statutory text has one California Supreme Court quotation. The categorical claim about employee non-solicits has one Court of Appeal decision, which does not support it as stated.
